points: The availability of Apple’s popular MacBook Air is being impacted due to the worldwide memory-chip deficit.

articles.title: Should you still buy your next smartphone — or subscribe to it instead?
articles.description: Apple's new Upgrade program is the latest sign that smartphone ownership is changing.
articles.summary: The article discusses how Apple's 'Upgrade Program' signals a shift in consumer behavior from outright purchasing new phones to subscribing for access.
points: Apple introduces the Upgrade program, allowing customers who paid full price for an iPhone or iPad before January 2018 to subscribe and get their devices replaced every year at a reduced cost.

The service is more affordable than buying new phones each cycle but comes with limitations on features such as unlocking the phone abroad, installing non-Apple apps, upgrading beyond three years old or transferring ownership without extra charges.
While not exclusively for Apple products and already offered by other companies like Samsung (OnSub), Microsoft's Bing Phone, Google Pixel Upgrade Service are still limited.
articles.insight: The trend towards subscribing to smartphone services rather than buying outright may continue as a cost-effective alternative for consumers and disrupt traditional sales models in the IT/technology industry. This approach could also influence how technology companies design, market, and sell their products.
